name: Singing Sand
description: A slope of sand that hums: grains slide at each key's pitch, fall into step until they sing one clear note, and come apart again as surges pass over the keys.

params.name: Lockstep
params.description: How many of the grains slide in step. Low is a breathing noise with a pitch in it, and at the top all of them sing one clear note.

params.name: Grain
params.description: How fine the sand is. Coarse grains give a dark round push at each slip, and fine ones a short bright one that hisses higher.

params.name: Grit
params.description: How rough each grain rubs. Smooth grains drift slowly past each other, and rough ones jump at every slip and put a rasp on the note.

params.name: Spread
params.description: How far off the note the grains want to slide. The ones Lockstep cannot hold beat around the pitch this wide.

params.name: Pulse
params.description: What kind of grain slips, each with its own hiss and its own way of coming to rest: round, flint, sand that squeaks, wet sand that pops, or ground glass.

params.name: Cluster
params.description: How many groups the grains lock into. The groups slip in turn, so two raise the octave of the note over it, three its twelfth and five a third two octaves up.

params.name: Layer
params.description: How strongly the sliding layer rings. It picks out one overtone of every key and sings it, with the hiss drawn into it.

params.name: Layer Order
params.description: Which overtone the sliding layer rings at. A deep layer takes the low ones, and a thin one whistles at the high ones.

params.name: Bury
params.description: How deep under the surface the slope is heard from. Deep takes the top off the sound and opens it only as a surge goes by.

params.name: Boom
params.description: The whole slope moving as one: a deep tone an octave under the key, or on it for the lowest keys, that is there only while the grains are in step.

params.name: Dry
params.description: How much loose dry sand runs along. First a soft hiss that follows the grains, then single ticks like far rain.

params.name: Surge
params.description: How the slope moves: in waves across the keys, in sudden bright slips that pass from key to key, or in one deep shock and rarer and rarer ones after it.

params.name: Slope
params.description: How steep the slope is. Steeper makes a surge rise further above the rest, and between two the grains come further apart. At zero the slide is even.

params.name: Pace
params.description: How often a surge comes. Slow ones swell and fade through a chord, and fast ones are a pulse.

params.name: Front
params.description: How a surge crosses the keys. With none all of them move at once, and with more it reaches one after the other and runs from side to side.

params.name: Onset
params.description: How long the grains take to gather when a key goes down, from a hiss to a note. Short is a strike.

params.name: Run
params.description: How long the first rush of a key lasts before it settles to what Flow leaves of it.

params.name: Flow
params.description: How much keeps sliding while a key is held. With none the sand runs out and the note ends by itself.

params.name: Slump
params.description: How long the slope takes to come to rest after a key is let go. The grains fall out of step and the note goes back to a hiss.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far across the stereo field the grains of a key lie, down to mono at zero. Grains out of step sound wider.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit after booming dunes and squeaking beaches. Each key is 24 noisy phase oscillators held together through their mean field, the textbook model of grains falling into step; the mean of their frequencies is held on the key. Each slip plays a pulse from a table built for its key with nothing above the band. Simplified: the layer is one resonator on an overtone of the key, the slope is a shared clock and not a flow, and the pulses are drawn and not measured. Nobody has listened to it: the constants were chosen by measurement.
